findings.title: Care returns through posture and prayer
findings.claim: With 17:23's aging parents in view, the lowered wing becomes voluntary protective softness: the grown child answers remembered nurture through posture and a spoken plea for mercy.
findings.mechanism: The focus's imperative to lower, its wing and humility images, its mercy request, and its words for parental raising and smallness meet 17:23's old-age setting and commands against rebuke and for noble speech. The context also makes the focus's say-command a continuation of careful speech. These contacts turn lowering from an abstract low status into present care answering an earlier period of dependence.
findings.reader_payoff: The body and the prayer become two forms of the same return: one who was once carried by parental care now bends and asks mercy for the parents.
findings.containment: The focus still commands lowering and asks for mercy. The pericope adds a life-course relation without making the parents objects of worship or requiring an identical repayment.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel supports the care and nurture relations, and the supplied immediate context names old age and restrained speech. The reading is bounded to this pericope contact and does not claim exclusivity.

findings.title: Aging care within worship and speech bounds

In 17:23, the parents' old age and ban on rebuke meet the focus's gentle lowering and memory of being small; the same verse reserves worship for God, while the focus turns its body toward the parents and directs its vocative and mercy request to the Lord. Alongside the initial construal, these contacts support a non-cultic, careful response to declining parental capacity.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold intense filial tenderness and a clear worship boundary together, while seeing speech restraint as part of the care offered.
findings.containment: The HFT reading is attributed and does not make the parents divine or claim that the sequence proves a strict life-cycle mechanism. The adjacent commands may teach etiquette without specifying reciprocal role transfer.

The focus's wing and active mercy then meet 17:26's due to near kin, 17:28's easy speech when giving cannot occur, 17:29's bound and fully extended hands, and 17:30's expansion and restriction of provision. Those independent contacts preserve the force of care while adding measured means: obligations remain, speech can carry mercy, and material giving has limits.

findings.containment: The resource rules may govern wider beneficiaries rather than parents specifically. This context bounds the filial reading; it does not make every unresolved HFT root a lexical sense of the focus.
